historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 company guidance (+3.0% revenue), cross-checked against equity 5yr CAGR 4.3% and post-break revenue 3yr CAGR 3.8%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (36%) diverges from equity CAGR (4.3%) by far more than 30%: FY2023 was still a COVID-recovery year and FY2026 EPS carries a JPY10.6bn one-off affiliate-sale gain. Not a growth signal. Revenue/EPS/FCF 5yr CAGRs are null because FY2021 is both the COVID trough (net loss JPY41bn, FCF -JPY30bn) and the last gross-basis revenue year; a CAGR across the FY2022 gross-to-net break is meaningless.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue 3yr: FY2023 487,407 -> FY2026 545,626 (both net basis). Equity 3yr: 546,120 -> 618,932; 5yr: FY2021 501,936 -> 618,932. Owner FCF 3yr: FY2023 48,012 - 0 SBC - 368 interest = 47,644 -> FY2026 58,908; reported-FCF 3yr CAGR is 7.7% so SBC is not eating into growth (SBC-zero market, understatement noted in sbc_source). The 4.3% equity CAGR flatters: it includes the FY2022-23 post-COVID rebound and retained one-off gains, so 3.0% is selected as the base-year growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Management delivers FY2027 guidance (revenue +3%, OP 84bn, capex ~39bn) and most but not all of the FY2025-2030 plan: the shift from mass store retailing to identified-customer / gaisho selling lifts the EBITDA margin from 19.1% to a 21% plateau by FY2032 (OP ~97bn in FY2030 against the 100-110bn Phase II target), while revenue growth decays from 3% to 1% as Japan's population shrinks and inbound spending stops compounding. Cash tax normalises from 18% to the 30.6% statutory rate by FY2029 as the post-COVID NOLs are used up, and capex runs at 6.5-7% of revenue through FY2029 for the Shinjuku remodels and DX before easing to 5.5%. The result is owner FCF dipping from JPY59bn (FY2026) to ~JPY48bn in FY2027-28 on the tax and capex step-ups, then rebuilding to ~JPY70bn by FY2036. Terminal value capped at 14x FCF (Gordon at 8%/1% would be 14.4x).
scenario_narratives.bull: The three axes all turn favourable: (1) inbound and HNW gaisho spending keep compounding (Q1 FY2027 identified-customer sales +6%, >JPY3m customers +16%, overseas app members ~1.1m) so revenue grows 4-4.5% through FY2029; (2) the kokyakugyo mix shift and cost programme take the EBITDA margin to 22.5%, delivering the 100-110bn Phase II operating-profit target on time (OP ~115bn by FY2030 in this path); (3) the machi-ka real-estate stream starts contributing by FY2030 and supports 1.5% terminal growth. Same WACC, same 14x cap -- the upside is in the flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 inbound dip was the warning, not the trough: a sustained yen rally or a Chinese travel-policy shock cuts duty-free and luxury volumes in FY2028-29 (revenue -1%/-2%), pricing power on the flagship floors fades and the EBITDA margin reverts to the FY2025 level of ~16.5% and stays there as regional-store decline and wage inflation offset the transformation gains. Growth settles at 0.5% and terminal growth at 0.5%. No solvency question -- net debt is ~0.3x EBITDA -- so this is an earnings-power bear, not a balance-sheet one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Isetan Mitsukoshi is valued as a mature, cyclical operating company on fully-taxed owner free cash flow: operating profit less normalised cash tax, less the elevated remodel capex the mid-term plan commits to, with the investment-securities portfolio and the pension deficit handled in the bridge rather than in the flows. The FY2026 base year flatters twice -- an 18% cash tax rate on NOLs that are almost used up, and a one-off affiliate gain in net income -- so the model rebuilds FCF from components rather than carrying FY2026 forward, and it deliberately gives management only partial credit for the 100-110bn Phase II operating-profit target in the base case. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, at a single 8% JPY WACC. The terminal multiple is capped at 14x FCF for a business that grows at ~1% in perpetuity; the market is currently paying ~21x trailing owner FCF and ~19x guided earnings, so the gap between model and price is largely the price of the inbound/luxury boom persisting and the machi-ka option.
key_risks_to_valuation: Inbound tourism / yen: overseas-customer sales are the swing factor in the margin path; FY2026 already showed a decline from the FY2025 record, and the bear case is a repeat with a harder landing
Cash tax normalisation is assumed fast (statutory by FY2029); if the group finds further shelter the base case is ~JPY40-60/share too low, if deferred-tax recoveries reverse it is slightly too high

Capex intensity: the ~100bn mid-term pool is modelled at 6.5-7% of revenue, but machi-ka redevelopment of the Shinjuku/Nihombashi blocks after FY2030 is excluded along with its returns -- a large real-estate build would make FCF negative for several years before paying back

Terminal multiple: the 14x FCF cap binds in base and bull; the market's current ~21x owner FCF implies either faster growth than modelled or a lower discount rate, and the model does not assume the re-rating persists
Equity-bridge assets: the securities portfolio (JPY45bn after haircut, ~JPY65/share) is carried at book for unlisted/equity-method stakes; its realisable value could differ materially either way
Revenue basis: FY2022's gross-to-net change means any external comparison of revenue growth or margins against pre-FY2022 figures is invalid; GMV (guided JPY1.36tn) is the like-for-like volume metric

inputs.sbc_source: ESTIMATE. Cash-flow statement carries no share-based payment add-back from FY2021 (exec LTI moved to a BIP stock trust that buys shares in the market; the P&L charge is inside SG&A and not separately disclosed). Yuho FY2026 remuneration table (3099.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:4737-4762) discloses JPY152m of PSU/RSU expense for holding-company officers only; subsidiary officers in the same trust are undisclosed. JPY350m is holdco disclosed plus a like amount for subsidiary executives, in line with the JPY240-370m consolidated SBC the cash-flow statement carried in FY2014-FY2020. Immaterial (~JPY0.5/share) but kept explicit per the house rule.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q1 FY2027 tanshin (2026-06-30, 3099.T_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:86-93): 367,449,054 issued less 18,695,280 treasury (incl. 817,936 BIP-trust shares) = 348,753,774 PRE-split, x2 for the 2-for-1 split effective 2026-10-01 = 697.5m, plus ~0.1% option dilution (diluted EPS 31.87 vs basic 31.90, split-adjusted) = 698.0m fully diluted POST-split. Price (2026-10-26) is post-split, so price and count are on the same basis; FY2027 EPS guidance of JPY92.48 is also post-split. Count held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and the buyback (JPY30bn / 36m post-split shares cap through 2027-02-08) is value-neutral in this model -- cash spent shrinking the count is cash not in FCF.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10y JGB ~1.7%, Japan ERP ~5.5%, beta ~1.1 for a department store operator whose profit pool is levered to inbound tourist / FX and domestic luxury cycles -> cost of equity ~7.8%; debt is ~5% of capital at ~1% after tax. WACC 8.0% applied to ALL three scenarios -- cyclicality, inbound/FX and transformation risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations 7f). Sits between the ~7% a pure CAPM gives and the ~9% house reference for JPY keiretsu industrials.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit (so inside EBITDA) and there are no material finance-lease obligations on the Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (3099.T_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:345-366 shows none). No lease adjustment; total_debt is short-term loans 17,092 + commercial paper 4,000 + bonds 20,000 + long-term loans 31,200 = 72,292 only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests JPY937m at 2026-06-30 -- trivial (0.15% of equity). Deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer'), with the non-US adaptations: JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases already expensed, NCI in the bridge, excluded-income/matching-asset rule applied to the investment-securities portfolio. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31): revenue 545,626; operating profit 80,020; D&A 24,430 -> EBITDA 104,450 (19.1%); capex 30,689 (5.6%); cash tax paid 14,419 (18% of EBIT); OCF 90,655; reported FCF 59,966; owner FCF = 59,966 - 350 SBC - 708 interest income = 58,908. REVENUE BASIS: FY2022 onward is net-basis (consignment sales moved from gross to net under the 2021 revenue-recognition standard, revenue roughly halved and gross margin roughly doubled); every growth and margin path here compounds from the FY2026 net-basis figure and no CAGR spans the FY2021/FY2022 break. NET INCOME FY2026 (76,096) included a JPY10.6bn gain on the partial sale of equity-method affiliate Shinkong Mitsukoshi; FY2027 net-income guidance (-17%) is that gain rolling off while operating profit is guided +5% -- the DCF runs on operating profit so the roll-off does not touch the flows. CASH TAX: FY2026's 18% cash rate reflects NOL usage; the NOL deferred-tax asset fell to JPY12,062m gross at 2026-03-31 with JPY9,830m valuation-allowanced (yuho:7794-7805), so the usable shelter is nearly gone and the path ramps to the ~30.6% statutory rate by FY2029. INTEREST INCOME stripped (708) and cash added in the bridge; dividend and equity-method income (6,292 in FY2026, smaller after the Shinkong sale) are outside operating profit already, so the securities that generate them go into the bridge at carrying value with a haircut. BUYBACKS: FY2026 financing outflow JPY35,110m plus JPY21,475m dividends -- the company funds a flat (actually shrinking) count, so the flat-count convention is paid for. GUIDANCE ANCHOR: FY2027 revenue 562.0bn (+3.0%), operating profit 84.0bn (+5.0%), capex plan ~38.7bn (yuho:2252); Q1 FY2027 operating profit +20.6% is tracking ahead of the full-year +5%.

bear.narrative: A yen rally and/or a China travel-policy shock in FY2028-29 repeats the FY2026 inbound dip but harder; EBITDA margin reverts to the FY2025 level (~16.5%) and the regional-store structural decline reasserts itself at ~0.5% growth.

base.growth_note: Year 1 = FY2027 guidance +3.0% (Q1 +3.8%, GMV guided +4.7%); then decays toward Japan nominal GDP as the domestic population shrinks and inbound growth normalises. Year-4 (FY2030) revenue ~608bn.
base.margin_note: FY2027 19.4% = guided OP 84.0bn + D&A ~25bn over 562bn. Rises ~0.4pp/yr on identified-customer mix, cost programme and the real-estate stream, plateauing at 21% (OP ~97bn in FY2030, just below management's 100-110bn Phase II target; the model does not give full credit for the plan).
base.capex_note: FY2027 plan ~38.7bn (6.9%, yuho:2252) for Shinjuku remodels and DX; held ~6.5-7% through FY2029 for the mid-term ~100bn investment pool, then eases to 5.5% (1.1x D&A) as remodel intensity normalises. Machi-ka redevelopment capex beyond FY2030 is excluded as are its returns.
base.tax_note: Cash rate 18% in FY2026 on NOL usage; the recognised NOL DTA is only ~2.2bn net of valuation allowance so the shelter is nearly exhausted. 26% FY2027 (FY2026 accrual of 16.7bn unpaid tax falls into FY2027 cash), 29% FY2028, statutory 30.6% from FY2029.
base.wc_note: FY2025 and FY2026 OCF both tie to EBITDA less cash tax within JPY1bn: payables float offsets card-receivable growth. Zero capture.

bull.narrative: Q1 FY2027 run-rate (OP +20.6%) proves to be the year, not a quarter: revenue beats guidance at ~+4.5% and the Phase II target is met (OP ~115bn by FY2030, 22.5% EBITDA margin by FY2033).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight down because the bull case needs three independent things to go right at once -- inbound/FX staying favourable, the kokyakugyo margin expansion actually reaching the Phase II target, and the machi-ka real-estate stream arriving on schedule -- and management itself frames FY2025-2030 as a 'preparation' phase. Bear weight up to 25% because the Analysis rates inbound/FX volatility a high-severity risk that already bit in FY2026, and department-store retailing is in secular volume decline; it is not higher because the balance sheet carries no refinancing risk (net debt 29bn against 104bn EBITDA) and the flagship real estate is a hard floor under the business.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.
